learning: Iteration 3 showed that lowering yaw inertia (with the lead restored) lifted s-bend progress from 0.04 to 0.75. Iteration 4 showed that the narrow track overshoots. Iteration 5 showed that reach is not the slalom limit. If the slalom still fails at max_error near 0.06 with line loss near 0, the next lever is controller kd or base_speed, not geometry.
notes: Iteration-3 geometry and controller, with mass reduced from 0.6 to 0.5 kg as the only change. This is the Builder's requested single-variable test of yaw inertia on the slalom.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (0.10 m track, 7 sensors at +/-0.06 m, lead 0.05 m, 0.6 kg, body 0.12 x 0.10 m, kd 0.6) scored 493.2, the best so far. It has zero s-bend line loss and progress 0.75, with an oval finish rate of 0.85. Iteration 4 showed that the 0.08 m track overshoots (s-bend oscillation 0.45, scores down to 355.9), so turn authority is not the limit. Iteration 5 showed that +/-0.07 m reach cut slalom and s-bend progress (score 430.1), so reach is not the slalom limit either. The slalom still ends off track at max_error about 0.062, at the 0.06 m floor. The Builder's requested change, mass 0.6 to 0.5 kg with the body unchanged, lowers yaw inertia by about 17 percent. I keep the iteration-3 controller (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.6, base_speed 1.4, proportional weights, last_direction) so that this race isolates mass. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.34 with some finishes, and oval and s-bend finish rates at or near iteration 3. Risk: lower inertia may raise s-bend steering_oscillation above about 0.5. Steering_oscillation is requested on every track so that this can be checked.
